newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Veba unit Deminex joins Caspian Azeri oil group.
newsitem.headline: Veba unit Deminex joins Caspian Azeri oil group.

text.p: Germany's Veba AG unit Deminex has joined an international oil consortium that will tap crude oil in Azerbaijan's sector of the Caspian Sea, the Assa-Irada news agency reported on Tuesday.

It said Deminex, with a 10 percent stake, would join France's Elf Aquitaine with 40 percent, Total with 10 percent, Agip SpA of Italy and Petrofina of Belgium each with five percent, and Iranian oil interests, whose stake is still under negotiation.
Azeri state oil company SOCAR also has a stake that may be split further.
The group will explore and develop on a production-sharing basis the Len-Koran and Talysh-Deniz fields.

The 30-year, multi-billion project south of the Azeri capital Baku involves fields containing up 140 million tonnes of recoverable oil. Peak output would probably reach 25 million tonnes a year (about 500,000 barrels per day).
